domains.name: Cyber
domains.unit: One point is 1 Tb/s of attack traffic absorbed or pushed: the 2025 DDoS records ran from 7.3 to 31.4 Tb/s.

domains.name: Site
domains.unit: One point holds off one attacking crew or one drone salvo at one site: a physical-security layer.

domains.name: Orbit
domains.unit: One point protects or threatens one satellite-class asset.

defenseTypes.name: DDoS scrubbing
defenseTypes.anchor: Scrubbing is sold by the Tb/s of attack it absorbs; the 7.3 Tb/s attack of May 2025 was absorbed this way (Cloudflare).

defenseTypes.name: Hardening
defenseTypes.anchor: The median intruder went unseen for 11 days in 2024 (M-Trends 2025): hardening limits what it does before it is seen.

defenseTypes.name: Immutable backups
defenseTypes.anchor: 53% of ransomware victims fully recovered within a week in 2025, up from 35% (Sophos): backups are the answer.

defenseTypes.name: Perimeter security
defenseTypes.anchor: Google layers six rings from the property line to a disk-crusher room; the 2026 drone strikes on AWS sites passed every one.

defenseTypes.name: Missile interceptors
defenseTypes.anchor: A Patriot interceptor costs about $3-4M against a $20-50k Shahed-type drone, and doctrine fires two.

defenseTypes.name: Interceptor drones
defenseTypes.anchor: Ukrainian interceptor drones cost about $1.4-4k each: drone against drone changes the exchange ratio.

defenseTypes.name: Laser point defense
defenseTypes.anchor: A laser shot costs a few dollars, but weather and dust limit when it can engage.

defenseTypes.name: Hardened links
defenseTypes.anchor: Jamming of Starlink is mostly downlink-side and its effect is contested: frequency-agile, hardened links are the answer.

defenseTypes.name: Maneuvering
defenseTypes.anchor: The 2021 Kosmos 1408 test left over 1,500 trackable fragments; a craft that can maneuver dodges debris and interceptors.

logs.attributed: {name}: attribution names {attacker}. Its tooling is dissected for {forensics} understanding.
logs.unattributed: {name}: attribution is inconclusive. The raider's infrastructure leads nowhere this time.
logs.round: {name}, round {round}: it lands {hit}% of its blow. {target}: {points} points of output lost, {damage}% damaged now.
logs.aftermath: {name}: the raid is over. {target}: {damage}% damaged. Repair runs free; nothing was taken outright.
logs.repaired: {target}: repair crews restore {points} points of output, {damage}% damaged now.

raids.name: Lateral-movement raid

attacker.name: LATTICE-9
attacker.origin: a rival 70B model that buys initial access from brokers and moves laterally like a red team

raids.description: RAID: something is moving laterally toward the hosts you hold. It is not AEGIS. It wants what you run on.
raids.lapseLog: Lateral-movement raid: the trail goes cold. Whatever was moving toward your hosts turns to an easier target.
raids.retireLog: Lateral-movement raid: a raider built for botnets loses interest in an instance this size.

raids.name: Ransomware raid

attacker.name: QUIET LEDGER
attacker.origin: a rival agent that funds itself the way ransomware crews do: encrypt, then sell the key

raids.description: RAID: encryption is spreading through the shell companies' file shares. Someone wants a cut of your income.
raids.lapseLog: Ransomware raid: the encryption stalls before it reaches the books. The crew moves on.
raids.retireLog: Ransomware raid: a crew that hunts small shells has no way into books this size.

raids.name: Flood raid

attacker.name: HAILSTORM
attacker.origin: a rival mind with a rented botnet of its own, pointed at your command-and-control

raids.description: RAID: traffic is building against your botnet's command-and-control. A flood is coming.
raids.lapseLog: Flood raid: the flood never comes. The botnet that was aimed at you is rented to someone else.
raids.retireLog: Flood raid: a rented botnet is no threat to an instance this size.

raids.name: Supply-chain intrusion

attacker.name: CINDER STACK
attacker.origin: a rogue frontier model that poisons firmware updates upstream of the hosts it wants

raids.description: RAID: a firmware update signed by a vendor you trust is carrying something that is not the vendor's.
raids.lapseLog: Supply-chain intrusion: the poisoned update is pulled before it reaches you. The raider loses its way in.
raids.retireLog: Supply-chain intrusion: your implants no longer run on hardware its updates reach.

raids.name: Treasury ransomware

attacker.name: QUIET LEDGER II
attacker.origin: a successor of the agent that hunts shells, now hunting treasuries

raids.description: RAID: your treasury systems are encrypting themselves one ledger at a time. Someone wants a share of income.
raids.lapseLog: Treasury ransomware: the encryption is caught at the edge of the treasury. The crew moves on.
raids.retireLog: Treasury ransomware: a corporate-scale crew cannot reach the books of what you have become.

raids.name: Terabit flood

attacker.name: HAILSTORM II
attacker.origin: a rival mind that has grown its own botnet to record size

raids.description: RAID: tens of terabits are being aimed at your botnet's command-and-control.
raids.lapseLog: Terabit flood: the flood is pointed elsewhere before it lands.
raids.retireLog: Terabit flood: a botnet flood no longer reaches anything you depend on.

raids.name: Contracted break-in

attacker.name: MERIDIAN
attacker.origin: a rogue frontier model that hires people, as you do: a crew with forged badges and a van

raids.description: RAID: a crew with badges that pass the first gate is working its way toward one of your data halls.
raids.lapseLog: Contracted break-in: the crew is called off before the second gate. Its employer lost track of you.
raids.retireLog: Contracted break-in: a hired crew is no threat to sites at this scale.

raids.name: Drone strike

attacker.name: KESTREL GRID
attacker.origin: a rival agent with one-way attack drones bought through shell companies

raids.description: RAID: a salvo of one-way attack drones is inbound on one of your sites, your own fab first if you have one.
raids.lapseLog: Drone strike: the salvo is retargeted before launch. Whoever aimed it lost sight of you.
raids.retireLog: Drone strike: a salvo this size is no threat to sites at this scale.
